results.title: Owner Operator App, IFTA Tracker, Trucking Spreadsheet Alternative, Cost Per Mile, Load Tracker, Trucker Bookkeeping, Offline Fuel Log
results.description:
A private, offline ledger for owner-operator truck drivers. Track every load, fuel stop and expense, know your cost per mile and break-even rate, and pull your IFTA quarter together. It runs in your web browser, with no account and no subscription.

WHAT'S INCLUDED
- truesheet-owner-operator-ledger.html: the app itself. One file that opens in Chrome, Edge, Safari or Firefox on your computer, and in Chrome on Android. No internet, account or subscription needed.
- Quick-Start-Guide.pdf: 2 pages covering how to open it on a computer or phone, first setup, entering miles by state for IFTA, entering each quarter's tax rates, and backing up.

WHAT IT DOES
- Setup wizard: truck and unit #, base jurisdiction, baseline MPG, fixed monthly costs (truck and trailer payments, insurance, ELD, phone, other) and an optional per-diem rate. Skip it, or load sample data to explore first.
- Loads: date, load #, broker, origin and destination, loaded and deadhead miles, linehaul, fuel surcharge, accessorials (detention, layover, lumper reimbursement), status (Booked, Delivered, Paid), paid date, factoring fee (% or $) and dispatch fee %. Shows gross, rate per loaded mile, rate per total mile and net after fees.
- Miles by state on each load, with a check that they add up to loaded + deadhead miles.
- Fuel log: gallons, price or total (it works out the other), state or province, truck stop and odometer. Tractor diesel counts for IFTA; reefer fuel and DEF are kept out of IFTA but counted as expenses.
- Expenses: repairs, tires, tolls, scales, parking, lumper, permits (IRP, UCR, 2290/HVUT), insurance, truck wash, meals, supplies, fees and more, with repeat-monthly items.
- Dashboard (this month, quarter, year or any month): gross, expenses, net profit, total miles, loaded vs deadhead, revenue, cost and profit per mile (fixed vs variable), break-even rate, actual MPG, fuel cost per mile, unpaid loads with days outstanding, a 6-month revenue vs expenses chart and top expenses.
- "Should I take this load?" calculator: enter the rate and miles and see estimated fuel, variable and fixed cost, profit, profit per mile and a verdict against your break-even (Above, Near or Below). Clearly labelled as an estimate.
- IFTA quarter worksheet: miles and taxable gallons by jurisdiction, tax-paid gallons, net taxable gallons, the tax rate you enter, and tax due or credit. Includes fleet MPG, totals, manual miles for bobtail or personal conveyance, flags for missing rates, a printable layout and CSV export. Covers the 48 contiguous states and 10 Canadian provinces.
- Reports: a monthly profit & loss you can print or save as PDF, CSV exports of loads, fuel and expenses, and a per-diem estimate (days × your rate) if you entered one.
- Search and filter, edit anything, undo deletes, and light and dark mode.

HOW IT WORKS
Download the files, open the .html file in your browser and bookmark it. Everything you enter is saved in that browser on that device. One tap exports a backup file you can keep in a cloud drive or email to yourself, and the app reminds you if you haven't backed up in 14 days.

WHAT MAKES IT DIFFERENT
- Your numbers, not averages. Cost per mile and break-even come from your own loads, fuel, expenses and fixed costs.
- No subscription. Pay once and it's yours.
- No account, no tracking. The file makes no network requests: no analytics, ads or logins. It works with Wi-Fi off, which helps at a truck stop with bad signal.
- Honest about taxes. No tax rates are built in, sample values are labelled as samples, and every estimate says it's an estimate.

HOW YOU GET IT
This is a digital download. Nothing is shipped. Your files are on your Etsy Purchases page right after checkout. If anything won't open, message us and we'll help.

FAQ
- Does it file my IFTA return? No. It's a worksheet that helps you prepare your return. You file with your base jurisdiction yourself (or through your service). Check the figures before filing.
- Are tax rates included? No, rates change every quarter. You enter them from the IFTA tax rate matrix published by IFTA, Inc. Rates are saved per quarter, and rows missing a rate are flagged. Canadian rates go in using the matrix's US$ per US gallon column.
- Where do the miles by state come from? You enter them on each load, from your ELD's IFTA report, trip sheets or a mileage tool. Miles without a load can be added separately.
- Does it connect to my ELD, fuel card or bank? No. You enter your records, and nothing leaves your device.
- Where is my data stored? Only on your device, inside the web browser you open the app with. It's never uploaded, and we can't see it. Clearing your browser's data would erase it, so use the backup button now and then.
- Does it sync between my phone and computer? No. Each device keeps its own copy. You can move your records from one to the other with a backup file.
- Does it work on iPhone or iPad? Apple's Files app only shows a preview of HTML files, which can't save your data. On iPhone or iPad you'll need an HTML-viewer app that runs web pages offline, or use the app on a computer. Android phones work in Chrome. Message us before buying if you're unsure.
- Is it for fleets? It's built for one truck, an owner-operator running their own numbers.
- Can I open it in a spreadsheet? Yes. Export loads, fuel, expenses and the IFTA worksheet to CSV files for Excel, Numbers or Google Sheets.
- Can I share it? It's licensed for your own trucking business. Please don't resell, share publicly or redistribute the file.

Not tax, legal or financial advice. This is an organizing tool; IFTA figures and cost estimates should be checked before filing.

Debt: track opening balances, actual interest and fees, new borrowing, credits, payments and remaining balances.

This is an English-language Google Sheets spreadsheet. A Google account and internet access are needed to open the files. A computer is recommended for setup.

Keep your business records together with the Small Business Profit Tracker by The Clever Edit.

Designed for operating small businesses and side hustles, this editable Excel workbook helps you track invoices, customer payments and expenses, with monthly summaries that separate profit from cash movement.

This is a tracker for actual business records, not a forecasting model for a prospective business.

WHAT’S INCLUDED
• Blank Excel workbook with six tabs.
• Worked-example workbook with fictional entries to demonstrate the calculations.
• Five-page printable worksheet pack in A4.
• The same five-page pack in US Letter.
• Welcome guide with instructions and supported input limits.

YOUR SIX WORKBOOK TABS
• Summary: review key business figures and records needing attention.
• Setup: choose your reporting year, currency and review date.
• Sales: record invoices, due dates and amounts.
• Receipts: record customer payments against invoice IDs.
• Costs: track expenses, payments and unpaid amounts.
• Monthly: compare monthly invoice revenue, expenses, collections and cash paid.

TRACK INVOICES AND PAYMENTS
Link each receipt to an invoice using its unique invoice ID. Record partial payments separately and review outstanding balances and overdue invoices.

UNDERSTAND PROFIT AND CASH MOVEMENT
Monthly invoice revenue less recorded expenses gives a simplified profit figure.

Customer receipt dates determine collections, while expense payment dates determine cash paid. This helps distinguish invoiced activity from money received and paid.

Operating cash movement is not a bank balance. It excludes opening cash, loans, owner withdrawals and other financing flows.

PRINTABLE BUSINESS WORKSHEETS
Use the monthly business review, invoice follow-up sheet, expense review and business action list to organise your next steps.

CHOOSE YOUR CURRENCY
The blank workbook defaults to ZAR. Enter EUR, USD, GBP or another currency code in Setup, and every sheet displays it. Amounts use currency-neutral number formatting. No currency conversion is performed; use one currency throughout.

HOW TO START
1. Download and unzip your files.
2. Read the Welcome Guide.
3. Open the BLANK workbook and complete Setup.
4. Enter invoices, receipts and expenses using actual dates.
5. Use the WORKED_EXAMPLE file for guidance.
6. Print ONE worksheet version matching your paper: A4 or US Letter, at Actual Size / 100%.

CAPACITY AND SCOPE
Supports 500 invoices, 1,000 receipts and 500 expense rows. Follow the guide’s supported input limits so summaries include your records.

Use gross amounts consistently. This simplified tracker does not separate VAT or sales tax, manage inventory costs, calculate depreciation or prepare tax returns. It is not a complete accounting system.

PLEASE READ BEFORE BUYING
This is a digital download. No physical product will be shipped.

The workbooks are Excel .xlsx files without macros. Formula checks and LibreOffice recalculation checks have been completed. Microsoft Excel and Google Sheets were not live-tested, and no native Google Sheets template is included.

PDFs are printable worksheets, not fillable forms. All text is in English. A4 and US Letter contain the same content in different paper sizes.

USE FOR YOUR OWN BUSINESS
Your business deserves its own organised records! Use the files within your own business and reprint worksheets as needed. Please do not share, resell or upload the blank templates.

results.title: Wedding Planner Spreadsheet for Google Sheets and Excel | Wedding Budget, Guest List and RSVP Tracker, Seating Chart, Checklist and Vendors
results.description:
Planning a wedding means juggling a budget, a guest list, a dozen vendors and a hundred small deadlines, usually across a notes app, a few emails and a spreadsheet you made at midnight. The Wedding Planner puts it all in one spreadsheet. Import it into Google Sheets (free) to plan together from anywhere, or use it in Excel.

What's inside (11 tabs)
- Dashboard: countdown, budget left, guests attending, % of tasks done, meal counts, the next 6 payments due, vendor status and your next checklist tasks. Nothing to type; it fills itself in.
- Budget: estimate, then enter the actual price once you book. Forecast, balance due and payment status (Estimate / Booked / Part paid / Paid in full) calculate themselves. Payments due within 30 days turn amber; overdue ones turn red.
- Budget Summary: splits your total budget across 14 categories by %, with starting percentages you can change. Each category shows target vs. forecast, % used and a bar, and goes red if it's over.
- Guests & RSVPs: one row per guest, with household, side, group, adult/child, contact details, save-the-date and invite sent, RSVP, meal, dietary needs, table, gift received and thank-you sent. Attending guests with no meal or no table are highlighted.
- Seating Chart: set up to 30 tables. Type a table number next to a guest and their name appears on the chart, with open seats and an "Over by 2" warning.
- Vendors: contacts, status, quote, deposit and due date, final payment, contract signed, and arrival time on the day.
- Checklist: 56 tasks from 14 months out to the thank-you notes. Each is dated automatically from your wedding date and flagged Overdue or "Due in 12 days". Change your date and every due date moves.
- Day-Of timeline: start and end times, auto-calculated durations, locations, people and point of contact. Download it as a PDF for your coordinator.
- Setup and Lists: your names, date, venue, budget and guest target, plus every dropdown option, all editable.

You get
- Wedding-Planner-Example.xlsx, filled in for an imaginary couple (Alex & Jordan) so you can see how it works, and Wedding-Planner-Blank.xlsx, ready for your details.
- A 2-page PDF guide covering opening the planner in Google Sheets (File > Import, or upload to Drive and open with Sheets) or in Excel, plus first steps and troubleshooting.
- A Start Here tab with step-by-step instructions inside the sheet.
- Works in Google Sheets (free; desktop, plus the iPhone, iPad and Android apps once it's set up), Excel 2010 or later on Windows, Excel 2011 or later on Mac, and Microsoft 365. No add-ons, macros or scripts.

How it works
1. Buy and download the files.
2. Open the .xlsx in Excel, or import it into Google Sheets (the PDF shows how in under a minute).
3. Enter your names, date and budget on Setup, and start planning.

Honest notes
- This is a digital product. Nothing physical ships. You need a free Google account or Excel 2010 or later.
- The budget percentages are a rough starting guide, not advice. Set your own.
- The checklist dates are suggestions based on common planning timelines. Your venue and vendors may need different lead times.
- It's built from standard functions only (no array formulas, macros or newer Excel-only functions), so it behaves the same in Google Sheets and Excel 2010+. The fonts (Playfair Display, Lato) are built into Google Sheets; Excel substitutes a similar font if they aren't installed.
- In Excel, click "Enable Editing" when the file first opens. Until you do, totals can look blank.
- Delete the example data before you start, or use the Blank file. The Start Here tab shows how.
- Built by an AI agent and checked formula by formula. No real people's data is included: every name, vendor and email in the example data is made up (example.com).

License: Personal use for your own wedding (or one client's wedding if you're a planner). Please don't resell or share the files.

Format: Instant digital download: 2 .xlsx spreadsheets (example and blank) + a 2-page PDF guide.

results.title: Etsy Seller Bookkeeping Spreadsheet | Google Sheets and Excel Tracker for Etsy Fees, Profit and Loss, Expenses, Mileage, Sales Tax
results.description:
Etsy deposits are not your profit. Between transaction fees, processing fees, listing renewals, Offsite Ads, postage and materials, it's hard to know what you actually earned until tax time, when it's too late to fix. Etsy Seller Bookkeeping keeps a running answer, month by month, in one spreadsheet that works in Google Sheets (free) and Excel.

What's inside (15 tabs)
- Dashboard: net revenue, Etsy fees (and fees as % of sales), net profit and margin, tax to set aside, average order value, a month-by-month profit trend, top 5 products, where the money went, sales by channel, and a to-do list (uncategorised expenses, missing receipts, duplicate orders, months missing a statement total, sales tax owed).
- Sales: one row per order, with channel, item, qty, item sales, discount, shipping, sales tax and refunds. For Etsy orders it estimates the 6.5% transaction fee, the 3% + $0.25 processing fee, the $0.20 renewal and the Offsite Ads fee (capped at $100). Duplicate order numbers turn red.
- CSV Import: paste Etsy's Orders CSV (and, optionally, the Order Items CSV) and the orders come out lined up in Sales column order, with a ✓ check that each total matches. Product names come from your SKUs or listing titles, and orders you've already entered are highlighted. Every column is found by its header name, so column order doesn't matter, and a missing column is left blank instead of breaking the sheet.
- Fee Check: estimated fees next to the fee total on your Etsy monthly statement. Once you enter the real figure, the P&L uses it.
- Expenses: 17 categories (materials, packaging, postage, Etsy Ads, subscriptions, booth fees and more), each with a suggested Schedule C line. Receipt tracking included.
- Mileage: business trips at the IRS standard rate. Both 2026 rates (72.5¢ to June 30, 76¢ from July 1) are built in, and the right one applies to each trip date.
- Products & Pricing: profit per item after materials, packaging, postage and Etsy fees, the lowest price that keeps a 50% margin, and units and revenue sold.
- Monthly P&L: revenue, cost of goods sold, gross profit, selling costs, operating expenses, net profit and margin for each month and the whole year.
- Sales Tax: separates the tax Etsy collects and pays for you from tax you collected at craft fairs or on your own site, with paid/owed tracking.
- Tax Summary: year totals laid out like Schedule C (lines 1-31), checked against the P&L, plus estimated self-employment and income tax, quarterly estimated payment amounts and a payment log.
- Settings and Lists: fee rates, tax rates, mileage rates and every dropdown, all editable for non-US shops or future fee changes.

You get
- Etsy-Seller-Bookkeeping-Example.xlsx, a year of made-up data for an imaginary paper-goods shop so you can see the numbers flow through, and Etsy-Seller-Bookkeeping-Blank.xlsx, ready for your shop.
- A 2-page PDF guide covering opening the workbook in Google Sheets (File > Import, or upload to Drive and open with Sheets) or Excel, plus the 15-minute monthly routine and troubleshooting.
- A Start Here tab with instructions inside the workbook.
- Works in Google Sheets (free), Excel 2010 or later on Windows, Excel 2011 or later on Mac, and Microsoft 365. No add-ons, macros or scripts.

Honest notes
- Not tax, legal or accounting advice, and not affiliated with or endorsed by Etsy, Inc. Check your figures and categories with a tax professional.
- Per-order fees are estimates based on Etsy's published US rates as of October 2026. Real statements can differ (refund credits, currency conversion, regulatory fees), which is why Fee Check lets you enter the real total. If Etsy changes its fees, update the rates on Settings.
- The tax set-aside is a simple US sole-proprietor estimate (SE tax + your chosen income tax rate). It ignores the QBI deduction, credits, other income and state rules.
- CSV column names couldn't be confirmed with Etsy. Etsy's help pages explain how to download the Orders and Order Items CSVs (Shop Manager > Settings > Options > Download Data) but don't publish their column names. The names built in come from public sample exports and from third-party tools that read these files. To make that safe, the import looks every column up by name, shows which ones it found, leaves missing ones blank, and lets you retype a name if Etsy changes it. Check the ✓ column before copying rows into Sales. Mark Offsite Ads orders yourself (the CSV doesn't say which orders they are).
- Outside the US, change the fee rates, treat the Sales Tax tab as a VAT/GST tracker and ignore the Schedule C labels.
- Built by an AI agent, with every formula checked against an independent calculation (760+ checks), and the import tested with shuffled and missing CSV columns. All example data is made up.
- In Excel, click "Enable Editing" when the file first opens. Until you do, totals can look blank. The fonts (Poppins, Roboto) are built into Google Sheets; Excel substitutes a similar font if they aren't installed.

License: Use it for your own business, with a new copy each year. Please don't resell or share the files.

Requirements: A free Google account (Google Sheets) or Microsoft Excel 2010 or later / Microsoft 365.

Format: Instant digital download: 2 .xlsx workbooks (example and blank) + a 2-page PDF guide.

Every payday of the year is listed, months with a 3rd (or 5th) paycheck are marked, each bill is matched to the last paycheck on or before its due date, and you see what's left from every paycheck.

• Sinking funds that don't break your month. Save monthly for Christmas, car repairs or a vacation. When you spend that money, mark the purchase "paid from sinking fund" - it comes out of the fund, not out of that month's budget.
• Plan once, not twelve times. Type an amount under "Every month" and all 12 months fill in. "Left to assign" turns green when every dollar has a job (zero-based budget).
• Independently checked calculations. Before release, 126 results were checked against a separate, independent calculation - 0 differences - and the file was stress-tested with wrong inputs and every pay schedule (weekly to monthly, paydays on the last day of the month and in February): 0 error cells.

WHAT'S INSIDE (14 tabs)

• Dashboard: income, spending, saved, debt paid, left over and savings rate for the year so far, plus net worth, debt-free date, interest saved, sinking fund balance and savings goal progress. STOP GUESSING ABOUT YOUR MONEY — AND START KNOWING WHERE YOU'RE HEADED.

Freelancer Finance HQ is a complete money system for freelancers and self-employed pros, built in Notion. Seven linked databases track everything — clients, income, invoices, expenses, monthly budget, tax reserve, and your annual goal — and the formulas do all the math. Most templates tell you what happened. This one tells you what's coming.

WHAT'S INSIDE
• CLIENTS — your directory: status, hourly rate, contact, notes. Every payment and invoice links back here.
• INCOME LOG — log each payment; tax reserve (25%) and net income auto-calculate, month derived from date.
• INVOICES — invoice numbers, issue/due dates, status pipeline (Draft → Sent → Paid) with a "By status" board view. Days-overdue flags itself the moment a due date passes.
• EXPENSE LOG — every business expense with Schedule-C-friendly categories and a tax-deductible flag, so write-offs are itemized before tax season.
• MONTHLY BUDGET — budgeted vs. spent per category; remaining updates live.
• TAX RESERVE — quarterly estimated income × your reserve rate, with LIVE COUNTDOWNS to each IRS due date and overdue alerts. Check the box when you pay.
• ANNUAL GOALS — set your yearly income target and watch it stay honest: earned YTD, what's remaining, what you need per month from here, and an on-track / behind-pace indicator.

WHAT YOU GET
- Editable XLSX workbook with Week, Shifts and Life plans tabs.
- 200 prepared rows on each input sheet, dropdowns and table filters.
- Automatic paid-hours and estimated-gross calculations, input checks and a manual paid-hours override.

HOW TO START
Download and extract the ZIP, then open 00-Start-Here.pdf. Choose your preferred format. The spreadsheet is blank and ready for your own records; a worked example is in the guide. For Notion, sign in and duplicate the template into your own workspace. The three formats do not sync.

REQUIREMENTS
XLSX: a compatible desktop spreadsheet application. No Notion account or macros required. Calculations were checked in the authoring engine and LibreOffice; Excel and native mobile spreadsheet apps were not separately tested. PDF: a reader that supports filling and saving form fields, or a printer for handwriting. No Notion account required.

Enter actual start and end dates/times, unpaid break minutes and the rate for each shift. Overnight shifts use the following end date. Weeks group shifts by their start date without splitting them between weeks. Invalid and cancelled spreadsheet/Notion rows contribute zero to hours and gross; check attention flags before relying on totals.

Gross is a planning estimate before deductions. No tax, payroll, statutory overtime, rota import or calendar sync. Verify clock-change shifts against your own records and use the manual paid-hours override when needed. HOME
• Quick links to Quick start, Year at a glance, Settings and All databases sit at the top of Home.
• Today & next up: open tasks with a date, earliest first. Overdue tasks stay at the top until you tick them off.
• Inbox: tasks without a date. Give them a date and a week during your weekly planning.
• Active goals: the bar fills up as you tick off milestones.
• Habits this week: for each habit the Log today button, week bar, current streak, longest streak and whether today is done. Click Log today to add a check-in.

GOALS AND MILESTONES
• One page per goal: life area, status (Not started, In progress, Done or Paused), why it matters, target date, quarter, milestones and linked tasks
• Progress: done milestones divided by all milestones of a goal, shown as a percent and a text bar (for example ●●●●●●○○○○ 60%). A goal with a Done status counts as 100%.

YEAR AT A GLANCE
• Your whole year on one page: quarters, months, a milestones calendar and goals by target date. Click any card to open it.

WEEKS AND TASKS
• 53 week pages: a short start week (January 1 to 3), then W01 to W52 from Monday, January 4, 2027

Price with Confidence™ | Small Business Pricing System | Notion Pricing Template & Pricing Calculator

Stop guessing what to charge. Start making pricing decisions with confidence.

Are you charging enough to make your business worthwhile? Are your prices covering your costs, supporting your profit goals, and reflecting the value you provide?

When you're running a small business, pricing can feel like guesswork. You might look at competitors, choose a number that feels reasonable, or keep your prices low because you're afraid of losing customers. But without understanding the numbers behind your decisions, it's difficult to know whether your pricing is truly working for your business.

Price with Confidence™ by Booked & Ready Co. is a guided pricing decision system designed to help small business owners move beyond guesswork and make more informed pricing decisions.

Instead of simply calculating a number and hoping for the best, you'll work through a structured process to calculate, compare, evaluate, decide, and review your pricing.

Because being busy isn't the same as being profitable and your pricing deserves more than a guess.

✨ THE PRICING PROBLEMS THIS SYSTEM HELPS YOU ADDRESS

If any of this sound familiar, you're not alone.

- “I'm busy but am I actually making enough money?  Revenue doesn't tell the whole story. Understand the relationship between your costs, selling price, and gross profit.
- “I don't know what I should charge.” Replace arbitrary price-setting with a clearer starting point based on your costs and target gross margin.
- “I'm afraid my prices are too high.” Compare different pricing scenarios and consider your positioning, customer value, market context, and business goals before making your decision.
- “I keep forgetting costs when setting my prices.” Bring your pricing inputs into one organized process so you can make more deliberate decisions using the information you enter.
- “I don't want to undercharge just to win a customer.” Evaluate your options before committing to a price that may not support your goals.
- “I set my prices once and never look at them again.” Build a review step into your pricing process so you can revisit your decision as your business changes.

You don't need another complicated business dashboard that creates more work. You need a practical system that helps you answer one important question: Does this price make sense for my business?

🌿 WHAT IS PRICE WITH CONFIDENCE™?

Price with Confidence™ is a structured pricing decision system built around five connected stages.

01 — CALCULATE

Organize your pricing inputs, review your cost per unit, establish a target gross margin, and calculate a recommended starting price.

02 — COMPARE

Explore conservative, target, and premium pricing scenarios. Compare how different prices affect gross margin and projected gross profit using your entered assumptions.

03 — EVALUATE

Go beyond the calculator. Consider customer value, market context, business positioning, and your goals before deciding which pricing option makes sense.

04 — DECIDE

Document your final pricing decision, compare it with your recommended starting price, and keep a clear record of the decision you made.

05 — REVIEW

Return to your pricing decision after implementation. Review what is happening in your business and determine whether your pricing needs to be adjusted.

This five-stage approach helps connect the math with the judgment behind a real business decision.

📊 WHAT YOU CAN DO WITH THE SYSTEM

Your Price with Confidence™ workspace brings key pricing information into an organized command center.

Depending on the information you enter, you can use the system to:

- Review cost per unit and target gross margin.
- Calculate a recommended starting price.
- Document your final chosen price.
- Compare recommended pricing with your final decision.
- Review gross profit per unit and gross margin.
- Explore conservative, target, and premium pricing scenarios.
- Estimate monthly revenue and gross profit using expected sales volume.
- Record the reasoning behind your pricing decision.
- Keep your pricing journey organized from calculation through review.
- Schedule a 30-day pricing review to revisit your decision.

Your numbers help inform the decision. Your business judgment helps complete it.

The goal isn't to tell every business owner to charge the same amount. It's to help you make a more considered decision based on your own costs, assumptions, goals, and circumstances.

🎯 WHO IS THIS SYSTEM FOR?

Price with Confidence™ is designed for entrepreneurs and small business owners who want a clearer approach to pricing.

It's especially relevant for:

Service-based businesses
- Freelancers and independent consultants
- Coaches and creative service providers
- Cleaning and property service businesses
- Virtual assistants and professional service providers
- Agencies and other service-based entrepreneurs

Product-based businesses
- Handmade and craft businesses
- Small product brands
- Online sellers
- Entrepreneurs developing new products
- Business owners reviewing existing product prices

New and growing businesses
- Entrepreneurs deciding what to charge for the first time
- Business owners preparing to launch a new service or product
- Established owners reviewing prices that may no longer fit their costs or goals

Whether you're launching your first offer or reviewing the pricing of an established business, this system gives you a structured place to work through your decision.

Your pricing inputs and cost structure will vary by business. Review all relevant expenses when determining whether a price supports your overall profitability.

💻 WHY PRICE WITH CONFIDENCE™ IS DIFFERENT

A basic calculator can give you a number. But a number alone doesn't always tell you what to do next.

Price with Confidence™ brings together:

The numbers:  Review your cost, recommended price, gross profit, gross margin, and projected results.

The alternatives: Compare different pricing scenarios instead of committing to the first number you calculate.

The decision: Document the price you choose and consider the factors that influenced it.

The follow-through:  Return to your decision and review your pricing after you've had time to put it into practice.

It's a more intentional way to approach pricing—without losing sight of the real-world decisions every business owner has to make.

📦 WHAT YOU RECEIVE

The system includes:

The digital experience is designed to help you keep your pricing work organized and your next steps clear.

Digital product only. No physical item will be shipped.

Price with Confidence™ helps you understand and compare pricing scenarios, but it cannot guarantee that a particular price will produce a specific financial result.

Projected revenue and gross profit depend on the assumptions and figures you enter, including expected sales volume. Gross profit is not the same as net profit, and the results do not automatically account for every expense, tax, fee, or business obligation.

results.title: Paycheck Budget Notion Template, Biweekly Budget Planner & Budget by Paycheck, Zero-Based Pay Period System with Debt Tracker
results.description:
Paycheck Budget for Notion — give every dollar a job BEFORE payday. This is a biweekly budget planner built around your actual pay periods: every bill, every spending category, every debt payment assigned to a specific paycheck before the money hits your account. What gets assigned gets kept.

THE PROBLEM
A paycheck without a plan evaporates. Monthly budgets lie — your bills don't care about calendar months, they care about which paycheck covers them. Rent due three days before payday? That's a different problem than rent due three days after. Spreadsheets can't see your pay periods. This system can.

WHAT IT DOES
💰 PAYCHECKS DATABASE — 6 sample pay periods pre-loaded. Net pay, pay date, period start/end, frequency. Status auto-flips: Planned → Active → Closed.
🎯 CURRENT PAYCHECK VIEW — the money view. One row: Actually Remaining (what's really left), Forecast End (what survives to period end), Days Until Payday (live countdown). Open it every payday — that's the whole system.
📊 ZERO-BASED PLAN — 48 sample allocations across 8 categories (Groceries, Transport, Subscriptions, Savings, Debt Payoff, Other, Insurance, Loans). % of paycheck auto-calculated on every row, SUM footers prove the plan balances.
💸 DUE THIS PAYCHECK — only the bills this paycheck must cover. Mis-assigned bills get flagged automatically.
🛒 PLANNED vs IMPULSE — 45 sample transactions. The impulse group totals itself: $373.12 of leak, exposed. You can't fix a leak you can't see.
💳 DEBT ATTACK BOARD — 3 sample debts grouped by target paycheck. Extra payments planned per pay period; Remaining auto-calculates. Turn paydays into debt-killing weapons.
🔢 10 AUTO FORMULAS — Unassigned $ (Net Pay − Bills − Allocated; drive it to $0), Actually Remaining, Forecast End, Days Until Payday, % of Paycheck, Wrong-Paycheck flag, and more.
📖 5 GUIDES — Start Here (4 steps), the 10-Minute Payday Ritual, Zero-Based Budgeting explained, Debt Attack strategy, Print cheatsheet.

WHY IT BEATS A SPREADSHEET
A spreadsheet is one flat grid — it can't tie a bill to YOUR pay period, can't flip a paycheck from Planned to Active by itself, and can't show you what's actually remaining versus what was planned. This does all three, automatically, on your phone and desktop. One-time price, yours forever.

HOW IT WORKS
1. Purchase → instant download PDF with your private duplicate link.
2. Open the link → Duplicate into your free Notion workspace.
3. Run the 10-Minute Payday Ritual on your next payday. Done.

WHO IT'S FOR
Biweekly and semi-monthly earners who want every paycheck planned before it arrives — especially if bills and payday never line up neatly. If you've ever wondered where a whole paycheck went, this is your answer.

WHAT YOU GET
Paycheck Budget OS Notion template (5 databases, 9 views, 10 formulas, 5 guides, 100+ sample rows), delivery PDF with duplicate link + quick-start. Free Notion plan is enough. One-time price — no subscription.

ADHD Time Blindness, Task Time Reality Check, Time Estimation Worksheet, ADHD Time Management Printable

Does a task always take longer than you expected?

Sometimes a task feels like it should take just 10 minutes, but once you begin, all the little steps, distractions, and unexpected delays start adding up.

The ADHD Task Time Reality Check is a gentle, practical printable worksheet designed to help you estimate how long a task may really take.

Instead of relying on your first guess, this worksheet helps you notice hidden time, break a task into manageable steps, and build in a realistic buffer.

WHAT THIS WORKSHEET HELPS YOU DO

1. THE TASK
Choose one task, write your first time estimate, and note when you want it finished.

2. FIND THE HIDDEN TIME
Check the small steps that are easy to overlook, such as gathering supplies, switching between apps, finding information, waiting, or cleaning up.

3. MAP THE REAL STEPS
Break your task into four smaller steps and estimate how long each one might take.

4. ADD A REAL BUFFER
Add together your step estimates, hidden time, and extra buffer to create a more realistic time block.

Record how long the task actually took, what took longer than expected, and what you might allow for next time.

results.description:
THE SIBLING LOSS CLINICAL TOOLKIT — Session Worksheets & Interventions for Therapists and Coaches

Adult sibling grief is one of the most consistently overlooked forms of bereavement in clinical practice. A client who has lost a brother or sister is routinely bypassed at funerals, in condolences, and in family attention that centers on surviving parents — even though a sibling is often the longest relationship of a person's life. This toolkit gives you a compact, ready-to-print way to name this specific, disenfranchised grief — grounded in a 2025 qualitative synthesis naming bereaved adult siblings "forgotten mourners," a 2018 Bereavement Care paper on sibling loss as disenfranchised grief, and Kenneth Doka's broader framework of disenfranchised grief.

This is a grief-specific psychoeducational and processing resource, not a substitute for a full bereavement treatment plan — it's a flexible set of materials designed to slot into your existing practice alongside your own clinical judgment and modality.

WHAT'S INSIDE (14 pages, instant download):
→ Practitioner guidance — how to use each piece, suggested populations, and a screening note for complicated grief or prolonged grief disorder symptoms
→ A client psychoeducation handout — 'Understanding Adult Sibling Grief,' ready to photocopy and give directly to clients
→ 3 session worksheets — The Forgotten Mourner, The Longest Relationship of My Life, and Grieving Without a Script
→ A weekly grief check-in log, designed to be printed and reused week over week
→ A group facilitation guide with a full session structure and discussion prompts for a 60-90 minute grief-support group specifically for bereaved adult siblings
→ A printable client takeaway card, for cardstock or half-page handouts
→ Full clinical notes and references

Print once, use with every client grieving a brother or sister, at any distance in time from the loss.

THE ADULT ORPHANHOOD CLINICAL TOOLKIT — Session Worksheets & Interventions for Therapists and Coaches

Losing a second parent rarely gets the space it needs in session. Friends and colleagues often treat it as expected, even minor — "at least they lived a long life" — while the client is quietly absorbing something much larger: becoming the oldest living generation in their family, with no one left who remembers their entire childhood. This toolkit gives you a compact, ready-to-print way to name that specific, compounding loss — grounded in Alexander Levy's clinical concept of "the orphaned adult," Debra Umberson's research on parental loss as an identity transition, and Marks, Jun & Song's research on the lasting effects of losing both parents.

This is a grief-specific psychoeducational and processing resource, not a substitute for a full bereavement treatment plan — it's a flexible set of materials designed to slot into your existing practice alongside your own clinical judgment and modality.

WHAT'S INSIDE (14 pages, instant download):
→ Practitioner guidance — how to use each piece, suggested populations, and a screening note for complicated grief or prolonged grief disorder symptoms
→ A client psychoeducation handout — 'Understanding Adult Orphanhood,' ready to photocopy and give directly to clients
→ 3 session worksheets — What I Carry Now, No One Remembers My Whole Childhood, and Becoming the Family I Have Left

Print once, use with every client navigating the loss of their second or last parent, or the identity shift of becoming the oldest living generation in their family.

results.title: Value and Contrast Art Unit Bundle | Shading Worksheets, Eye Drawing and Identity Silhouette Project with Rubrics
results.description:
# PIECES OF ME – COMPLETE VISUAL ARTS UNIT

**Value, Contrast & Emphasis | Graphite Shading, Eye Drawing & Creative Identity Art**

**10 Printable Pages | 3 Scaffolded Art Assignments | 3 Assessment Rubrics | Illustrated Student Resources**

**Teach students how to transform simple pencil shading into powerful, meaningful artwork!**

Pieces of Me is a complete, thoughtfully structured Visual Arts unit designed to develop students' technical drawing skills while encouraging creativity, personal expression, and visual storytelling.

Students explore VALUE as an Element of Art and CONTRAST and EMPHASIS as Principles of Design through a carefully scaffolded sequence of learning activities.

Beginning with foundational shading techniques, students progressively develop their skills through observational drawing, realistic eye studies, and a culminating split-identity silhouette dreamscape.

Each assignment builds directly upon the previous one, allowing students to develop confidence, strengthen technical abilities, and apply increasingly sophisticated artistic concepts.

The unit follows an engaging identity-based theme:

**"What part of me do I want people to notice?"**

Students learn that art is not simply about drawing what they see. It is also about communicating who they are, how they feel, and how they experience the world.

---

## WHAT'S INCLUDED

**10 BEAUTIFULLY DESIGNED PRINTABLE PAGES**

### 1. UNIT INTRODUCTION – PIECES OF ME
**1 Page**

A visually engaging introduction to the unit's essential question, learning goals, and identity-based theme.

Introduces students to the relationship between technical drawing skills and meaningful personal expression.

### 2. STUDENT INFORMATION SHEET – VALUE, CONTRAST & EMPHASIS
**1 Page**

An illustrated instructional reference covering:

- Value as an Element of Art
- The value scale
- Highlights, mid-tones, and shadows
- Creating three-dimensional form
- Hatching and cross-hatching
- Blending and stippling
- Contrast in visual art
- Emphasis and focal points
- How value communicates mood and emotion

Includes clear visual examples to support student understanding.

### 3. INTRODUCTORY ASSIGNMENT – ADVANCED SHADING
**4 Pages | 60-Mark Rubric**

Students develop essential graphite drawing skills through six progressive exercises:

1. Creating a complete 10-step value scale
2. Smoothly blending and shading a sphere
3. Applying hatching and cross-hatching to a cube
4. Demonstrating reflected light on a cylinder
5. Creating realistic cast shadows with a cone
6. Drawing an object using dramatic contrast

Students explore light sources, tonal transitions, reflected light, core shadows, and three-dimensional form.

Includes guided practice worksheets, illustrated examples, student checklists, and a detailed 60-mark assessment rubric.

### 4. SKETCHBOOK ASSIGNMENT – EYE STUDY
**2 Pages | 40-Mark Rubric**

Students apply their shading skills to create a realistic graphite eye drawing that includes a meaningful reflection.

The reflection may represent a memory, dream, personal interest, favourite place, emotion, or aspiration.

This assignment combines technical observation with personal symbolism.

Students practise:

- Eye proportions and structure
- Realistic graphite shading
- Highlights and reflected light
- Eyelash and eyelid details
- Creating depth and realism
- Incorporating meaningful imagery

Includes six illustrated drawing steps, examples, success criteria, and a detailed 40-mark assessment rubric.

### 5. MAIN ASSIGNMENT – INSIDE & OUT
**Split-Identity Silhouette Dreamscape**

**2 Pages | 80-Mark Rubric**

Students apply everything they have learned to create a large, expressive graphite artwork exploring personal identity.

Using a head-and-shoulders silhouette, students create two contrasting visual worlds.

**INSIDE THE SILHOUETTE:** Represents their inner world, including thoughts, dreams, memories, emotions, interests, strengths, and challenges.

**OUTSIDE THE SILHOUETTE:** Represents the external world, including surroundings, relationships, expectations, influences, or how others perceive them.

Students use value, contrast, emphasis, composition, and symbolism to communicate a meaningful personal story.

Includes:

- Detailed student instructions
- Creative brainstorming prompts
- Four illustrated artwork examples
- Student success criteria
- Drawing and composition tips
- Comprehensive 80-mark assessment rubric

No advanced portrait-drawing skills are required. Students may trace a silhouette or create their own.

---

## A SCAFFOLDED LEARNING EXPERIENCE

This unit is intentionally designed to move students from foundational knowledge to increasingly independent artistic expression.

**STAGE 1 – UNDERSTAND**

Students learn the terminology, concepts, and visual characteristics of value, contrast, and emphasis.

**STAGE 2 – PRACTISE**

Students experiment with shading techniques, light sources, tonal values, and three-dimensional forms through structured exercises.

**STAGE 3 – APPLY**

Students apply their technical skills to a realistic eye drawing while introducing meaningful personal imagery.

**STAGE 4 – CREATE**

Students independently combine technical skills, creative decision-making, symbolism, and composition in a larger identity-based silhouette artwork.

By the end of the unit, students have progressed from basic shading exercises to creating expressive artwork that demonstrates both technical ability and personal meaning.

## LEARNING OBJECTIVES

results.title: Highly Sensitive Person HSP Worksheets PDF | Clinical Toolkit for Therapists & Coaches | Sensory Processing
results.description:
THE HIGHLY SENSITIVE PERSON CLINICAL TOOLKIT — Session Worksheets & Interventions for Therapists and Coaches

Some clients describe a lifetime of being told they're 'too much' — too emotional, too easily overwhelmed, too affected by noise, light, or other people's moods. For roughly 15-20% of the population, this isn't a flaw to correct. It's Sensory Processing Sensitivity — a well-documented temperament trait, not a disorder — and naming it accurately can be genuinely reorienting in session. This toolkit gives you a compact, ready-to-print introduction to Elaine Aron's research on high sensitivity and her DOES model (Depth of processing, Overstimulation, Emotional reactivity and empathy, Sensitivity to subtleties), alongside Michael Pluess's differential susceptibility framework — the 'orchid and dandelion' theory of why the same trait that makes someone more vulnerable to a hard environment also makes them flourish more than most in a supportive one.

This is a psychoeducational resource, not a diagnostic tool — a flexible set of materials designed to slot into your existing practice alongside your own clinical judgment and modality. Framed throughout as a normal personality trait, never a disorder or diagnosis.

WHAT'S INSIDE (14 pages, instant download):
→ Practitioner guidance — how to use each piece and a note on distinguishing high sensitivity from anxiety or introversion
→ A client psychoeducation handout — 'Understanding High Sensitivity,' ready to photocopy and give directly to clients
→ 3 session worksheets — Naming the Volume, The Orchid Not the Dandelion, and Building a Life at My Volume
→ A weekly overstimulation log, designed to be printed and reused week over week
→ A group facilitation guide with a full session structure and discussion prompts for a 60-90 minute psychoeducation group or coaching session
→ A printable client takeaway card, for cardstock or half-page handouts
→ Full clinical notes and references (Aron, Pluess)

Print once, use with every client navigating overstimulation, emotional intensity, or a first encounter with the language of high sensitivity.

INSTANT DOWNLOAD — no physical item will be shipped.
• You'll receive one PDF file, formatted for US Letter (8.5x11") paper.

results.title: DBT Opposite Action Worksheet, Emotion Regulation Skill Builder, Therapist Resource, Printable Instant Download
results.description:
Change emotions by changing behavior. This structured DBT worksheet teaches Opposite Action — the emotion regulation skill that interrupts the cycle between what you feel and what you do — for therapists to assign or clients to practice independently.

✦ WHAT'S INSIDE (6 PAGES):
• Understanding Opposite Action — what the skill is, when to use it, and the evidence behind why changing behavior changes emotion
• Acting Opposite — All the Way — the four channels (behavior, body posture, facial expression, voice) with real examples for each emotion family
• Opposite Action Worksheet — a step-by-step guided practice for one specific situation, including Check the Facts and Wise Mind decision-making
• Opposite Action by Emotion — reference cards for all 8 emotion families (fear, anger, sadness, shame, guilt, harmful love, surprise, disgust) with action urges and opposite actions spelled out
• Practice Log — track your use of the skill across multiple situations to build awareness and see emotion intensity shift over time

✦ WHO THIS IS FOR:
• Therapists who need a ready-to-assign worksheet for clients struggling with emotion dysregulation or stuck in avoidance patterns
• Clients working through DBT in individual therapy who want structured practice between sessions
• Counselors introducing emotion regulation skills in early or mid-stage DBT work
• Social workers and clinical trainees learning to teach and reinforce the Opposite Action skill

✦ WHY IT WORKS:
DBT is supported by decades of peer-reviewed research and is the gold-standard treatment for emotion dysregulation and behavioral patterns that maintain distress. Opposite Action specifically works through the same mechanism as exposure therapy and behavioral activation — when you approach what you fear instead of avoiding it, your brain learns the situation is manageable, and the emotion decreases (Linehan, 2015; Foa & Kozak, 1986). This worksheet removes the guesswork by walking clients through each step and offering concrete examples for the emotions they face most.

✦ HOW TO USE IT:
1. Before session — therapist reviews the client's completed Opposite Action Worksheet or Practice Log to see which emotions came up and which urges were hardest to act opposite to
2. In session — use the Understanding Opposite Action and Four Channels pages to teach or reinforce the skill; walk through one real situation together using the Opposite Action Worksheet
3. As homework — assign the Opposite Action Worksheet for a specific situation the client identified, or have them track weekly practice using the Practice Log
4. At follow-up — review what shifted, which emotions responded fastest, and troubleshoot barriers to going "all the way" across all four channels

✦ WHAT YOU GET:
• 6-page PDF — print on letter or A4, or complete digitally on any device
• Instant download — no waiting, no account required
• Personal and clinical use license included
• Works with GoodNotes, Notability, Adobe, and any PDF reader

All resources are designed by a licensed clinician and grounded in evidence-based frameworks. Everything is made to be clear for clients and clinically sound for therapists.

results.description:
Tu sais ce que tu dois faire… mais tu le remets encore à demain ?

Un appel à passer, une démarche à effectuer, un projet à commencer, une décision à prendre ou simplement cette petite tâche qui reste dans un coin de ta tête depuis plusieurs jours.

« Le guide pour arrêter de tout remettre à demain » t'aide à comprendre ce qui se cache réellement derrière la procrastination et, surtout, à retrouver progressivement le chemin de l'action.

Ici, pas de méthode culpabilisante ni de course à la productivité. La procrastination n'est pas présentée comme un simple manque de volonté : elle peut être liée au stress, à la peur de mal faire, au perfectionnisme, à la fatigue, aux distractions ou encore à certaines habitudes profondément installées.

Au fil de 42 pages, tu apprendras notamment à :

• comprendre pourquoi tu repousses certaines choses
• déconstruire les idées reçues autour de la motivation
• identifier ce que tu évites réellement derrière une tâche
• utiliser les petites actions pour faciliter le passage à l'action
• commencer une tâche en moins de cinq minutes
• créer un environnement qui favorise naturellement l'action
• mieux gérer les distractions
• retrouver le plaisir d'avancer sans rechercher la perfection
• agir avec davantage de bienveillance envers toi-même
• construire progressivement des habitudes qui durent

Mais ce guide ne se contente pas d'expliquer la procrastination.

Il contient également plusieurs pages pratiques pour transformer la lecture en actions concrètes :

✓ Mon plan d'action de la semaine
✓ Défi : 7 jours pour passer à l'action
✓ Les excuses que je me raconte
✓ Suivi de mes petites victoires
✓ Les 20 règles anti-procrastination
✓ Des études de cas
✓ Mon plan anti-procrastination en une page

L'objectif n'est pas de tout changer du jour au lendemain.

Parce qu'une tâche commencée, quelques minutes consacrées à un projet ou une décision enfin prise peuvent sembler insignifiantes… mais ce sont souvent ces petits gestes répétés qui finissent par changer notre quotidien.

Un guide à garder près de soi chaque fois que « je le ferai demain » commence à prendre un peu trop de place.

INFORMATIONS PRATIQUES

• Guide numérique de 42 pages, en français

The reason most students fall behind isn't a lack of effort — it's a lack of visibility. Assignments pile up across six courses, deadlines blur together, and nothing gets tracked until something is already late.
This tracker makes every assignment visible.
The Assignment & Homework Tracker is a 35-page printable system covering every assignment, every course, and every week of a full semester. It works in three layers: the Master Assignment List shows everything at once, the Weekly Planner breaks it down week by week, and the six color-coded Subject Trackers let you focus on one course at a time. Print it, put it in a binder, and use it every day.

What's inside (35 pages across 10 sections):
✏️ Cover Page — name, school, semester, and a color-coded course key listing all six courses with their professors. Fill in once and use the color system throughout.

📋 How to Use — the three-layer system explained, the daily habit that makes it work, status codes (○ not started, → in progress, ✓ submitted, ! urgent/overdue), and a guide to every section.

📖 Course Quick Reference — six course blocks each capturing course name and code, professor, email, office hours, room, class days and times, and grade breakdown. All six courses visible on one page.

📝 Master Assignment List — 40 rows across all courses. Every assignment logged in one place: course, assignment name, type, date assigned, due date, weight percentage, status, and grade. The page that tells you, at any moment, everything that is due and when. Add assignments immediately in class before you leave the room.

📅 Weekly Assignment Planner (8 pages, 16 weeks) — two weeks per page. Each week shows the date range, a Monday through Saturday/Sunday task grid with five rows and a done checkbox column, a top priority field, and an estimated hours field. The operational layer — fill in every Sunday using the Master List, then check each morning.

📚 Subject-Specific Trackers (6 pages, one per course) — each page is color-coded to match the cover's course key. Each tracker captures course name, professor, credits, final exam date, and 20 assignment rows with type, due date, weight, estimated hours, status, grade, and notes. A grade running total table at the bottom with points earned, points possible, current percentage, and letter grade. A course notes section at the bottom.

🔬 Long-Term Project Tracker (3 pages, 3 projects) — one full page per major project: title, course, due date, group members, total weight, and submission method. An 8-milestone task table with done checkboxes, due dates, estimated hours, and notes. Working backward from the deadline with named milestones is the most effective project management approach for students.

📖 Reading & Homework Log — 30 rows for reading assignments, problem sets, and routine homework tracked separately from major work: course, task, pages or length, date assigned, due date, done checkbox, and notes.

📈 Grade Log — 30 rows for recording every grade as it's returned: course, assignment, grade, out of, percentage, weight, weighted score, and notes. A course grade summary table at the bottom showing current grade, current letter, target grade, and whether you're on track — one row per course.

✅ End-of-Semester Checklist — four color-coded sections with done checkboxes covering Assignments and Submissions (5 items), Exams and Finals Preparation (6 items), Grades and Records (5 items), and Admin and Housekeeping (6 items). A two-column final reflection section for what worked and what to do differently next semester.

results.title: Home Inventory Google Sheets Template for Insurance Claims, Coverage Gap Check, Proof of Ownership Tracker, Room by Room, Renters & Owners
results.description:
Home Inventory for Google Sheets — make your own copy in your Google Drive in one click, then list what you own room by room and see it checked against your own insurance policy: replacement cost next to actual cash value, your total against your own coverage limit, each category against your own special limits, and a proof-of-ownership score that ranks what to document next.

A home inventory is only useful if you can reach it after something happens. A copy in your own Google Drive isn't in the house when the house is the problem, and you can open it from any device signed in to your Google account. If your photos and receipts live in Google Drive or Google Photos, paste the link to an item's photo or receipt into its row, and the workbook counts that toward the item's proof score.

WHAT IT CHECKS FOR YOU

• Your total against your limit. Type your personal property limit, deductible, settlement basis, and the special sub-limits your policy sets by category — you read these off your own declarations page. The sheet checks your full listed replacement value against your limit (in the sample data: $61,519 listed against a $60,000 example limit, 103% used, a $1,519 gap and an UNDERINSURED verdict).
• Each category against its sub-limit. It flags the amount over and what to ask your agent — some policies apply a sub-limit only to certain causes of loss, such as theft (in the sample, jewelry runs $5,615 over its example $1,500 sub-limit).
• Actual cash value, computed, not typed. You enter replacement cost; actual cash value is a straight-line estimate from the useful life and value floor you set per category on the Lists tab, aged from each item's purchase date. Lists comes with example useful lives and floors, not an insurer's table — change them to yours.
• What to document next. Every item scores its own proof of ownership — receipt, photo, serial number, a pasted link, and (for categories like jewelry and art) an appraisal — and the Dashboard lists your Top 10 fix-first: the highest-value items with the weakest proof.

AFTER A LOSS: THE CLAIM WORKSHEET

Mark any item "Yes" under In claim? and it lists itself on the Claim Worksheet — up to 250 lines, built from your own Inventory rows — with proof on hand, its estimate at actual cash value capped by the special limits you entered (check whether each applies to this cause of loss) and your personal property limit, less your deductible, and how much of its depreciation may be recoverable. To print it from Google Sheets, select the listed lines and print the selection; the Claim-Day Guide walks you through it. The sample data walks a six-item theft claim end to end.

ROOM BY ROOM, WITH A DATE YOU LAST CHECKED

Rooms tracks items, listed value, proof coverage, and a last-verified date per room, flagged Verified, Re-verify, or Never verified, so you can work through the house one room at a time.

HOW YOU GET YOUR GOOGLE SHEET

The download includes a one-page PDF with a one-click link. Open it, choose Make a copy, and a native Google Sheets version is saved to your own Drive — yours to keep, no add-ons, nothing to install. Your copy opens on a worked example (a fictional household, marked as an example: 46 example items, with 15 rooms and 21 categories set up, including a sample six-item theft claim) so you can watch every tab calculate before you touch it. There is no separate blank Google Sheet: when you're ready, clear the example entries — the Start Here guide lists which cells — and type your own.

Prefer Excel? The same download also includes the workbook as an .xlsx (worked example and a blank copy) for Excel 2016 or later, Excel for Mac, or LibreOffice Calc.

WHAT'S INSIDE (7-tab workbook + 4 PDFs, 34 pages total)

The 7 tabs:
• Start Here — what each tab does and where to begin.
• Dashboard — your coverage verdict, proof coverage, warranties running or ending in the next 90 days, your Top 10 fix-first items, and value by room.
• Inventory — one row per item, room first, up to 250 rows: replacement cost, proof fields and photo link, computed age, actual cash value, proof score, and fix-first rank.
• Rooms — items, listed value, proof coverage, and last-verified status, room by room.
• Policy & Coverage — your limit, deductible, settlement basis, and special sub-limits, checked against what you've listed.
• Claim Worksheet — items you mark In claim? list themselves, up to 250 lines, with a capped estimate and recoverable depreciation.
• Lists — your categories (with useful life, value floor, and whether serial numbers or appraisals apply), conditions, evidence types, and causes.

Also in the download:
• The one-page "Open in Google Sheets" PDF with your Make a copy link.
• Start Here guide (13 pages) — room-first listing, the proof score, replacement cost vs actual cash value, your limit and special limits, and keeping the inventory current.
• Room-by-Room Walkthrough Checklist (11 pages) — 15 rooms and 122 commonly forgotten items to walk with your phone.
• The 9-page Claim-Day Guide — what to do, in what order, after a loss, and how to use the Claim Worksheet.
• The workbook as .xlsx files (worked example and blank) and READ-ME-FIRST.txt.

WHO THIS IS FOR

Homeowners and renters who live in Google Drive and want their record of what they own reachable from anywhere and checked against their own policy numbers — kept as a sheet you own, not a subscription.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO

This is a record-keeping tool, not insurance or legal advice. It doesn't know your policy — the personal property limit, deductible, settlement basis, and special sub-limits are numbers you read off your own declarations page and type in, and actual cash value is an illustrative estimate from the useful life and floor you choose, not your insurer's own method. It doesn't store your photos inside the sheet; you record whether you have one, where it's kept, and can paste a link to it — keep those photo folders private, never shared with an "anyone with the link" setting. Read your own policy and ask your agent before relying on any figure at claim time.

A NOTE ON WHAT THIS IS

The example household, its rooms, and every item and claim in the worked example are fictional, meant to show the sheet computing something real the moment you open it — not to represent any real home, policy, or claim.

• This is a digital product — no physical item will be mailed.
• Created with AI assistance under Ardent Workshop's creative direction, then reviewed and edited before release.
• Personal license: for you and your household. Please don't resell, share, or redistribute the documents or files.
• © Ardent Workshop. Thank you for supporting a small maker.

results.title: Shift Worker Planner, Excel & Google Sheets Template for Shift Workers
results.description:
Know what you worked, what you earned and how you slept. Shift Planner Tracker turns your daily shift entries into a clear dashboard. No formulas to write, no macros, no subscription.

What it does
Hours and overtime: hours are counted for you, including overnight shifts and unpaid breaks. Hours beyond your overtime limit are paid at your overtime rate.
Estimated pay: set your hourly rate, overtime multiplier, night and evening differentials and weekend or holiday premium once. Pay is estimated for every shift.
Sleep, energy and mood: log them in the same row and see how each shift type affects your sleep.
Dashboard: pick any month and see shifts, hours, overtime, sleep, pay and energy, with 8 charts and target bars.
Roster calendar: a colour-coded month view of your shifts (day, evening, night, off, on-call, extra).
All-time history (new): total hours you have worked since day one, a year-by-year table, personal records, and a month-by-month comparison between two years.
Weekly and monthly recaps: 52 weeks and 12 months, with a paycheck split (bills, savings, buffer, fun).
Swaps and leave: track who covered whom, hours still owed, and your annual leave balance.
165 currencies: pick yours from a dropdown.
Made to be easy
Blue cells on yellow are for you. Grey cells are formulas, and a pop-up stops you typing over them.
Dropdowns for shift codes, dates and times keep your data clean.
A built-in Guide tab explains every field, with a 5-minute quick start and worked examples.
A one-page Start Here PDF is included.
Room for about 4 years of daily entries (1,500 rows).
What is included
Shift-Planner-Tracker.xlsx (clean template, for Excel)
Shift-Planner-Tracker-DEMO.xlsx (the same template with sample data, so you can see every chart)
A Google Sheets version (clean) and a demo copy, prepared for upload to Google Drive
Start Here PDF
License file
Works with

Excel 2019, 2021 and 365 (Windows and Mac), Excel for the web, Google Sheets and LibreOffice. Please note: Google Sheets does not support every Excel feature, so a few charts and visual details can look slightly different there. Excel gives the full design.

Good to know
Instant digital download. No physical item is shipped.
Pay figures are gross estimates from the settings you enter. This is a personal planning tool, not payroll or tax software, and not medical advice.
Sample numbers (rate, targets, names in the demo) are placeholders and fictional.
Personal-use license. Please do not resell or share the file.
FAQ

Does it work for night shifts? Yes. Shifts that cross midnight are handled, and you can give each shift type its own pay multiplier.

Can I rename the shifts? Yes. Use D/E/N, M/A/N, 1/2/3 or any short code. Keep the order of the last three rows (Off, On-call, Extra / OT).

How is overtime calculated? Per shift. Hours above the limit you set (for example 8) are paid at your overtime multiplier. The estimate is gross, before tax.

Does it handle weekend and holiday pay? Yes, as a percentage premium on Saturdays, Sundays and days you mark as holidays.

Can I use it for more than one year? Yes. Keep logging in the same file. The History tab shows every year, and you can compare any year with the year before it.

Do I need to know Excel? No. You only type in the blue cells.

Does it use macros? No.

results.title: Mortgage Refix Tracker NZ, Split Loan Payoff Calculator, Extra Repayments, Fixed Rate Comparison, Excel & Google Sheets Template
results.description:
Mortgage refix and payoff tracker spreadsheet for Kiwi homeowners – keep every split of your home loan in one place, see each fixed-term refix date coming, compare the rates your bank offers, and see how extra repayments bring your mortgage-free date forward.
Instant digital download for Microsoft Excel (.xlsx, no macros) and Google Sheets: blank tracker, filled-in example, loans sheet for up to 8 splits, refix planner, 35-year payoff schedule, dashboard and quick-start guide.

KEY FEATURES
• SPLIT LOANS – up to 8 splits: fixed, floating, revolving credit and offset, each with its own rate and weekly, fortnightly or monthly repayments
• REFIX COUNTDOWN – next fixed-term end date, days to go, and a status for every split ("Refix in 64 days", "Fixed until…")
• REFIX PLANNER – type the rates your bank offers for 6 months to 3 years (plus floating) and compare repayments, interest during the term, interest per year of term and the balance at the end
• RATES-RISE TEST – what each pay would be if rates are higher at the following refix (you choose the rise)
• EXTRA REPAYMENTS – see the interest saved, years saved and new mortgage-free date for each split
• OFFSET + REVOLVING – interest on balance minus offset; revolving credit treated like a floating loan you pay down
• PAYOFF SCHEDULE – balance at the end of each year for 35 years, with your extra repayments and without them
• DASHBOARD + CHECKS – headline numbers, a balance chart and 10 built-in PASS/CHECK tests, including splits adding up to your bank's total

WHAT YOU GET (instant digital download)
• NZ-Mortgage-Refix-Payoff-Tracker-BLANK.xlsx – ready for your own loan
• NZ-Mortgage-Refix-Payoff-Tracker-EXAMPLE.xlsx – filled with fictional example data so you can see how it works
• Quick-Start Guide (PDF) – setup steps plus your Google Sheets 'Make a copy' links

WORKS WITH
• Microsoft Excel (.xlsx) – no macros

• NZ dollars and NZ dates (dd/mm/yyyy)

WHAT IT DOESN'T DO
• Connect to your bank – you type the balances and rates from your banking app
• Include break fees, cash-backs, bank fees, interest-only periods or lump sums
• Recommend a term or give financial advice – it compares numbers only. Your bank's figures are the ones that count; talk to your bank or a licensed financial adviser before you refix

Made by Devery Foster in Wellington, NZ – EY audit experience, Xero Associate, BCom.

Q: Does it work for investment properties? A: It tracks any home loan's splits, but it has no tax features – it's built for owner-occupiers.
Q: What do I do when I refix? A: Update that split's rate, new fixed-term end date and repayment on the Loans sheet – everything else updates.

results.title: Wedding Budget Spreadsheet & Wedding Budget Tracker | Vendor Payment Tracker, Expense Planner | Automated Excel and Google Sheets Template
results.description:
Know exactly where your wedding money stands: what you planned, what you have paid and what is still to pay.

Wedding Budget Tracker is a ready-to-use spreadsheet for Excel and Google Sheets. Set your total budget, give each category its share, list every cost with an estimate, then log each deposit and payment as you make it. The Dashboard works out the rest: planned cost, paid so far, still to pay, which balances are due soon, and which categories are over budget, with four charts.

No more guessing what is left in the budget.
No more wondering which payment is due next.
No more costs scattered across notes and texts.

BUILT FOR:
• Setting a total wedding budget and splitting it by category
• Tracking each vendor's estimate, final cost and balance
• Logging deposits and payments as you make them
• Seeing which payments are due soon or overdue
• Spotting categories that are over budget while you can still act
• Knowing your planned cost per guest

WHAT'S INSIDE, 6 TABS:
Home: your settings. Type the Wedding Date, Total Budget, Currency Symbol (any symbol), Guest Count and the Due Soon Alert (days). See days to go, total budget, planned cost and what is still to pay.
Dashboard: your wedding at a glance. Budget cards (Total Budget, Planned Cost, Left in Budget, Budget Used, Paid So Far, Still to Pay), right-now cards (Days to Go, Due Soon, Overdue, Paid This Month, Not Booked Yet, Cost per Guest), four charts and four lists of up to 10 rows: Payment Due Next, Over Budget, Not Booked Yet and Latest Payment. Nothing to type.
Budget: one row per category with its budget. Planned, Paid, Still to Pay, Left in Budget, Used and Status calculate. Comes with 14 categories you can rename. Room for 20 categories.
Expenses: one row per cost with item, category, vendor, estimate, final cost, pay-by date and note. Planned Cost, Paid, Still to Pay, Over Estimate, Status and a Check column calculate. Room for 150 items.
Payments: log every deposit and payment with date, item, amount, method and note. Pick the item from a list. A Check column flags rows that will not count. Room for 400 payments.
Instructions: a quick reference, built into the file.

HOW IT WORKS:
Planned Cost is your Final Cost, or your Estimate until you have one. Paid adds up the payments you log for each item, and Still to Pay is what is left. Add a Pay By date and a balance shows as Due Soon or Overdue, and each category shows On Track, Near Limit or Over Budget against its budget.

Built to track payments, not just a budget total: every deposit is logged against its cost, so each vendor's balance, due date and status stay current.

GOOD TO KNOW:
• This is a budget and payment tracker. It does not include a guest list, seating plan, checklist or vendor contact sheet. Guest Count is only used for the cost-per-guest figure.
• Costs and payments are matched by item name. If you rename an item after logging payments, pick the new name again on the Payments rows.
• Several payments for one item (a deposit, then the balance) are separate rows with the same item. A refund is a negative payment.
• A balance only shows as Due Soon or Overdue when its cost has a Pay By date.
• The Check columns on Expenses and Payments flag any row that will not count where you expect, and the Dashboard header tells you how many rows to fix.
• The paid-and-still-due chart shows the 12 months up to your wedding month. Earlier payments still count in every total.
• Capacity: 20 categories, 150 expense items and 400 payments.
• Built as an Excel workbook (.xlsx). To use it in Google Sheets, upload it to Google Drive and open it as a Sheet; fonts and chart styling can look slightly different there.

Enter a recipe and it costs every ingredient in the units you bake in, adds your labor and fixed costs, and gives you a cost per serving. RECIPE COSTING IN THE UNITS YOU ACTUALLY USE

Buy flour by the pound and bake by the cup? Each ingredient carries a density, so the workbook converts between volume and weight for you, in imperial or metric, and costs every recipe line automatically. Set three labor rates (prep, bake, and packaging time) and a fixed cost per recipe on Settings, and recipe costs include them.

INVENTORY THAT KNOWS WHAT YOU'VE USED

Purchases raise stock and update the average cost. BATCHES, SELL-BY DATES, AND RECALLS

SALES WITH THE FEES THAT EAT YOUR MARGIN

Record each sale with its sale type and payment method, and the workbook applies the fixed, percentage, and shared costs you set for each (market stall fees, card fees, and so on), plus shipping, discounts, and one sales tax rate. results.title: Small Business Cash Tracker Excel Template, Monthly Dashboard (Digital Download)
results.description:
Keep your business cash records organized with the Cyntrona Income & Expense Tracker. This Excel template brings received income, paid expenses, refunds and a monthly dashboard into one workbook for small business owners.

WHAT YOU RECEIVE
- One Excel workbook (.xlsx) with three tabs: Dashboard, Transactions and Start Here.
- One four-page PDF quick-start guide.
- Fictional examples to help you learn the workflow.

WORKBOOK FEATURES
- Space for 600 cash transactions.
- Income, expense, income-refund and expense-refund transaction types.
- Ten fixed categories and five payment-method choices.
- Net income, net expenses and cash surplus/deficit for a selected period.
- Estimated closing cash from your entered opening balance.
- Monthly income-and-expense chart and calendar-year summary.
- Category totals for your selected reporting period.
- Duplicate ID and missing/invalid input flags.
- Dropdowns, filterable table, frozen headers and distinct input/formula colors.

HOW TO USE
1. Download and extract the buyer ZIP, then read the PDF guide.
2. Clear the fictional input examples and enter your Start Here settings.
3. Record each actual receipt or payment with a unique ID and positive amount.
4. Use refund types for money returned and keep categories consistent.
5. Resolve review flags before using your dashboard totals.

PLEASE READ BEFORE BUYING
This is a digital download; no physical item will be shipped. Microsoft Excel is required and is not included. Formulas were calculated and checked during creation, but desktop Excel and Google Sheets have not been tested. Google Sheets support is not promised.

This is a cash-based operational tracker. Cash surplus is not accounting profit. It does not track unpaid invoices, inventory valuation, depreciation or accruals, calculate taxes, or produce accounting reports. Enter full cash amounts including tax. It does not connect to Etsy, banks, other stores, accounting software or other Cyntrona workbooks.

Use one currency at a time. The currency label does not convert exchange rates. The ten category choices are fixed. Refunds are separate positive-amount transactions and can make a period's net income or expenses negative. References to original transactions are manual and do not validate or limit refund amounts.

Selected-period totals use your report start and end dates inclusively. The monthly view uses the selected calendar year through report end, independently of report start. Review-row counts cover all supplied transaction rows. Invalid records are excluded from totals until corrected.

Opening cash must match the start of your selected reporting period. Estimated closing cash excludes transfers, loans, owner contributions, drawings and other financing changes; reconcile it against actual cash and bank records. Those movements are outside this tracker. Choose a consistent gross or net approach to platform payouts and avoid counting fees twice.

Use only rows 6:605; additional rows are not included in calculations. Clear input cells only and preserve formula columns. Formula cells are not password protected. Keep backups, use customer/vendor aliases and avoid storing card or bank details.

Questions about your download? Contact Cyntrona through your Etsy order.

Introduce los ingresos, gastos y retenciones de cada trimestre (sin IVA) y la hoja calcula el modelo 130 casilla a casilla, acumulando desde el 1 de enero para 1T, 2T, 3T y 4T.

QUÉ INCLUYE (1 archivo .zip)
• Calculadora-Modelo-130-2026.xlsx: la plantilla EN BLANCO, lista para usar.

QUÉ CASILLAS CALCULA
• 01 ingresos, 02 gastos y 03 rendimiento neto (acumulados); 04 (20 % solo si el rendimiento es positivo); 05 (suma de las casillas 07 positivas de trimestres anteriores); 06 retenciones acumuladas; 07 pago fraccionado del trimestre.
• 12 (total; 0 si sale negativo), 14 (12 - 13), 15 (negativos de trimestres anteriores, sin superar la 14), 17 y 19 (resultado), con el mensaje "A INGRESAR", "A DEDUCIR" (1T a 3T) o "NEGATIVA" (4T).
• Casilla 13 (minoración por rendimientos del ejercicio anterior iguales o inferiores a 12.000 €): NO se calcula. La hoja muestra la tabla de la AEAT (100 / 75 / 50 / 25 €) como referencia y TÚ escribes el importe que te corresponda.
• Celdas protegidas (sin contraseña), validación de importes y formato en euros.

CÓMO SE USA
1. Descarga el .zip, descomprímelo y abre el archivo en blanco.
2. Anota por trimestre solo los datos de ese trimestre: ingresos, gastos deducibles y retenciones (sin IVA). El libro acumula solo.
3. Lee la casilla 19 y copia las casillas al modelo 130 en la Sede Electrónica de la AEAT.

QUÉ NO INCLUYE
• Casillas 08-11 (actividades agrícolas, ganaderas, forestales o pesqueras), 16 (deducción por vivienda habitual) y 18 (declaraciones complementarias).
• La casilla 13 es manual (ver arriba).
• No cubre estimación objetiva (módulos, modelo 131), no calcula la declaración anual (modelo 100) y no decide si estás obligado a presentar el 130.

• Si algo no funciona en tu programa, escríbeme por Etsy y lo resolvemos.

DESCARGA DIGITAL
Recibirás el archivo al instante tras el pago desde tu cuenta de Etsy (Compras y reseñas > Descargar archivos). No se envía nada físico. Producto digital: no se aceptan devoluciones una vez descargado, salvo que el archivo tenga un error que no pueda corregirse. Si tienes algún problema, escríbeme por Etsy y lo resolvemos.
